title: Automation of the Micronucleus Assay Using Imaging Flow Cytometry and Artificial Intelligence
protocol: Acquire imaging flow cytometry data.
Count cells using a commercially available cell counter before culture and after recovery period for non-Cyt-B method.
Place Brightfield (BF) in Channel 4 on single camera imaging flow cytometer.
Use the 40x magnification during acquisition.
Set X-coordinates to 100 and 900, Y-coordinates to 0.7 and 1 on BF area versus BF aspect ratio plot for Cyt-B method.
Set X-coordinates to 100 and 600, Y-coordinates to 0.7 and 1 on BF area versus BF aspect ratio plot for non-Cyt-B method.
Set X-coordinates to 55 and 75, Y-coordinates to 9.5 and 15 on Hoechst intensity plot for Cyt-B method.
Set X-coordinates to 55 and 75, Y-coordinates to 13 and 21 on Hoechst intensity plot for non-Cyt-B method.
Remove images of apoptotic and necrotic objects from data using IDEAS 6.3 software package.
Ensure the image analysis software is up to date.
Save work as a template (.ast) file.
Create .daf files for all .rif files through batch processing.
Select Add Batch under the Tools menu in the AI software.
Add .rif files to be processed in the batch window.
Select the .ast file that was created previously.
Assign a batch name if needed and click on OK to create .daf files.
Launch the AI software and ensure the most recent version is installed by clicking on About.
Choose where to save the experiment using the Folder icon.
Type a name for the experiment (e.g., "MN model").
Start a training experiment by clicking the Train radio button.
Proceed to the next screen.
Select a previously trained model as a template if available.
Skip selecting a template and proceed by clicking Next if no previous model exists.
Populate the Define New Model screen with the model name from step 3.3.
Optionally type a description for the model.
Leave the maximum image size at 150 pixels.
Add a brightfield channel under Channels, rename it to BF.
Add a fluorescent channel and rename it to DNA.
Click on Add under Class Names to add Mononucleated class.
Type Mononucleated in the pop-up window and click OK.
Repeat the process to define Binucleated, Binucleated with MN, Polynucleated, and Irregular morphology classes.
Proceed to the next screen by clicking Next.
Right-click on one of the truth populations and select Select All Matching Populations to add tagged populations from multiple files to the appropriate class.
Click on Next.
On the Select Channels screen, choose BF to channel 1 and Hoechst to channel 7.
Right-click on a channel and select Apply to All.
Click on Next.
On the Confirmation screen, click on Create Experiment.
The AI software loads images from the data files and creates model classes defined in step 3.5.3 with the ground truth imagery that was assigned in step 3.7.
Click on Finish.
Click on Tagging to launch the tagging tool interface.
Click on the zoom tools (magnifying glass icons) to crop the images for easier viewing.
Adjust the image size by clicking on the slider bar to change how many images are shown in the gallery.
Choose Min-Max from Display Setting options to provide the best contrast image for identifying all key events.
Change the color of the DNA image to yellow or white by clicking on Setup Gallery Display, which improves visualization of small objects such as MN.
Run the clustering algorithm by clicking on Cluster to group objects with similar morphology together.
Select individual clusters listed under Unknown Populations after clustering is complete and view objects within each cluster.
Assign selected objects to their appropriate model classes.
Continue assigning a minimum of 25 objects to each model class until the Predict algorithm becomes available.
Click on Predict once sufficient objects are assigned to each model class for accurate predictions.
Populate ground truth model classes with appropriate imagery until at least 100 objects have been assigned in each class.
Train a model using Random Forest and CNN algorithms by clicking on Train after reaching the Training tab.
Right-click on Channel 1 and click Apply to All for brightfield imaging.
Right-click on Channel 7 and click Apply to All for DNA staining.
Click Next to proceed without assigning truth populations if not required.
On the Confirmation screen, click Create Experiment to load the selected model and images from chosen data files.
Click Finish after creating the experiment.
Click Classify to launch the classification process using RF and CNN models.
Select checkboxes for RF and/or CNN models as needed before beginning classification.
Once classification is complete, click View Results to review outcomes.
Click Update DAFs button to update .daf files with new classifications.
On the Results screen, click Generate Report to create a summary of results.
Select Create Report for Each Input DAF if individual reports are desired.
Click OK to save and open report files in designated folder.
Calculate relative population doubling using appropriate formula and data.
Calculate cytotoxicity for each sample using the CBPI from control cultures (C) and exposed cultures (T).
Use counts in mononucleated, binucleated, and polynucleated classes from class_count.csv file to calculate Cytokinesis-Block Proliferation Index (CBPI).
